key_insight: Error-Conditioned Neural Solvers feed the PDE residual directly into the model so it can learn how to iteratively correct its own prediction errors, instead of relying on residual minimization as an optimization objective.
engineering_relevance: This enables faster, more accurate PDE surrogates that are more robust under distribution shift while avoiding the heavy compute and instability of classical hybrid optimization methods.
method: Input the current residual field at each iteration as a signal of spatial error structure.
Train a learned update policy to refine predictions iteratively rather than solving an inner optimization problem.
Target correction under ill-conditioned PDE regimes where low residual does not reliably imply low solution error.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports evaluation across four PDE families, with ENS achieving the highest accuracy in most settings, up to 10× gains on turbulent Kolmogorov flow, and strong zero-shot transfer under parameter and cross-equation shifts.
watch_item: Performance likely depends on how well the residual field is computed and represented; noisy or poorly discretized residuals could weaken the learned correction policy.
